scope: Two fixed interpreted CPU-loop stability cases; this does not establish full stability, physical-device, reader-feature or G4 acceptance.

implementation.ordinaryPayload: Small reflection bridge only; the test helper is absent and the operation explicitly returns CPU_LOOP_PROBE_NOT_PACKAGED.
implementation.diagnosticPayload: Opt-in helper uses actual public createSession/execute/cancel/closeSession APIs and the original unchanged Rhino engine/job observer.
implementation.workload: Complete 16384 JavaScript iterations with checksum 402644992, publish a unique nonblocking signal, then run arithmetic forever without further host or Java calls.
implementation.cpuProof: After the signal, independently sample the actual worker in Interpreter.interpretLoop with no signal, NativeJavaMethod, SourceJavaHost or dispatchHost frames. Signal arrival alone never passes.
implementation.deadline: Each child retains its own original public RuntimeTask deadline and is rejected if that actual deadline exceeds the parent. Parent cancellation propagates through public cancel; public execute deadline semantics are unchanged.
implementation.recovery: Require distinct CANCELLED and TIMEOUT envelopes, context exit and a successful public evaluate returning 42 on the same owned worker, followed by session close and worker termination.

nativeAcceptance.status: Native execution pending; desktop validation does not satisfy an iOS acceptance gate.

requiredEvidence: Authenticate enclosing source, platform, launch PID and checkpoint time before checking the CPU result.
Require exactly one public-cancel and one absolute-deadline case with distinct UUID signals, task/session/recovery identifiers and original public envelopes.
Require actual iteration/checksum evidence, a later positive interpreter stack sample and public cancellation after that sample.
Reject a host-handshake-only stack or substituted explicit cancellation for the natural deadline case.
Verify every child deadline, same-worker recovery, context exit, isolated session close, worker stop and empty owned workload registry.
limitations: The registryEmpty field covers this diagnostic's owned workload registry; it does not claim every global runtime registry is empty.
The existing host-handshake cancellation case remains unchanged and is separate evidence.
Network/browser cancellation, sustained sessions, concurrency coverage and physical-device performance still need separate validation.
